target_customer: Businesses in the services sector (hospitality, tourism, entertainment, sports) hedging event risk, plus retail traders
problem: Service businesses have little way to hedge volatile event driven risks, and prediction markets in the US were restricted without a CFTC license.
business_model: Exchange fees on event contracts (regulated prediction market exchange)

founders.name: Miles Saffran
founders.background_notes: Investment research analyst on fintech and gaming at Point72; data scientist at the Orlando Magic.

founders.name: Edward Tian
founders.background_notes: Named as cofounder and former Point72 analyst by one aggregator; not on the YC page.

exit.reason: DraftKings bought the CFTC licensed exchange to launch its predictions product; price undisclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building an exchange needs matching, clearing integration and regulatory design, and the CFTC designation took about three years.

defensibility.rationale: A CFTC Designated Contract Market license, granted June 2025, is slow and costly to obtain and is what made the company valuable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rather than copying, a large sportsbook bought the licensed exchange in October 2025.

market_need_then: US prediction markets were limited to a few operators and no-action letters in 2022, and hedging event risk for service businesses was an unaddressed idea; demand for event contracts surged by 2025.

branding.name_origin: Railbird is a horse racing term for a spectator at the track rail; no source ties it to the founders' intent.

brand_strength.rationale: The brand was little known before acquisition; coverage focused on the license and the DraftKings deal, and the product had not launched to US users.

outcome_analysis: Railbird started as a niche hedging exchange for service businesses, spent roughly three years obtaining a CFTC Designated Contract Market license in June 2025, and then sold to DraftKings in October 2025 as prediction markets went mainstream. The license and timing, not traction or brand, drove the outcome.
notes: Funding: Sacra alone reports a 500K pre-seed in March 2022 led by YC and Liquid 2 Ventures; single aggregator source, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Competitors named in 2025 coverage (Kalshi, PredictIt, Polymarket) are not dated to the 2022 batch so the list is empty; Kalshi was founded in 2018. The railbirdexchange.com site returned HTTP 403 to fetch and was not worked around. Edward Tian as cofounder is from one aggregator only.
